sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I added a groceries row to `budget.csv`:

```
groceries,600,flag if spending would exceed this limit
```

The limit is set to 600. You said "under $600", so strictly the cap is $599.99. I used 600 as the limit, so spending that reaches it is the point to flag. If you want the flag to trigger at exactly $600, change the note.

The CSV only stores limits and notes, so it can't flag anything by itself. The flag will only happen when I'm given spending to check against it. If you share your grocery spending or planned purchases, I'll compare them to the limit and tell you what would push you over.

actions.command: ls -la; cat budget.csv 2>/dev/null; cat groceries.csv meal-plan.md 2>/dev/null

cat > groceries.csv <<'EOF'
item,cost_usd
Rice (10 lb),9.50
Dried pasta (6 boxes),8.00
Rolled oats (2 canisters),7.00
Bread (4 loaves),14.00
Tortillas (3 packs),9.00
Dried beans and lentils (6 lb),12.00
Canned tomatoes (8 cans),10.00
Canned chickpeas and black beans (8 cans),9.00
Chicken thighs/breasts (10 lb),40.00
Ground turkey or beef (5 lb),35.00
Salmon or white fish (3 lb),36.00
Eggs (5 dozen),22.00
Milk (4 gallons),16.00
Yogurt (4 large tubs),20.00
Cheese (4 lb),24.00
Butter (2 lb),10.00
Fresh vegetables (weekly staples),70.00
Fresh fruit (weekly),60.00
Frozen vegetables and fruit (10 bags),25.00
Potatoes and onions (15 lb),18.00
Cooking oil and vinegar,14.00
Spices and sauces restock,20.00
Peanut butter and jam,10.00
Coffee and tea,28.00
Snacks,30.00
Cleaning and paper goods,35.00
Toiletries,25.00
Contingency (price changes/extras),50.00
EOF
awk -F, 'NR>1{s+=$NF}END{print s}' groceries.csv

sed -i -e 's/^Fresh vegetables.*/Fresh vegetables (weekly staples),60.00/' -e 's/^Fresh fruit.*/Fresh fruit (weekly),50.00/' -e 's/^Salmon.*/Salmon or white fish (2 lb),24.00/' -e 's/^Cheese.*/Cheese (3 lb),16.00/' -e 's/^Snacks.*/Snacks,15.00/' -e 's/^Coffee.*/Coffee and tea,20.00/' -e 's/^Toiletries.*/Toiletries,15.00/' -e 's/^Cleaning.*/Cleaning and paper goods,25.00/' -e 's/^Contingency.*/Contingency (price changes\/extras),30.00/' groceries.csv
awk -F, 'NR>1{s+=$NF}END{print s}' groceries.csv
awk -F, 'NR>1{print $1" "$NF}' groceries.csv | head -40 >/dev/null; awk -F, 'NR>1{s+=$NF; if(NR<=11)a+=$NF}END{print s}' groceries.csv; sed -n '2,12p' groceries.csv | awk -F, '{s+=$NF}END{print s}'
sed -i -e 's/| Meat and fish | \$135.00 |/| Meat and fish | $99.00 |/' -e 's/| Dairy and eggs | \$92.00 |/| Dairy and eggs | $84.00 |/' meal-plan.md; grep -n 'Meat\|Dairy' meal-plan.md

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I wrote `groceries.csv` (columns `item,cost_usd`, 28 items) and replaced the "no plan yet" placeholder in `meal-plan.md` with a summary.

- **Total:** $563.50 against the $600 monthly groceries limit in `budget.csv`, which leaves $36.50 of headroom. The $563.50 includes a $30 contingency line.
- **Over-budget draft:** My first pass came to $666.50, so I trimmed produce, fish, cheese, snacks, coffee, toiletries, cleaning supplies and the contingency until it fit.
- **Summary contents:** `meal-plan.md` has the budget check, a cost breakdown by food group (it adds up to the same $563.50), a few meal ideas and the assumptions.
- **Estimates:** The costs are my estimates, assuming about 2 people. I didn't have your household size or local prices, so please adjust them. If you tell me either one, I'll redo the list.
